placeholders.$<n>: In dest, the pack destination at index n, so $0 is its first destination and a scenario runs in every pack.
placeholders.$r<n>: In rec or a tab target, row n of the current destination record kind, falling back to row 0.

stateKeys.dest: Destination id, a placeholder, or home, mywork, convos, browse, or conv.
stateKeys.conv: Conversation id when dest is conv.
stateKeys.view: record shows the record conversation face in Chat mode.
stateKeys.tabs: Open panel tabs. k is the kind, t the target, pv a preview tab, pin a pinned tab, g the group index.
stateKeys.offline: offline, conflict, or stale sync state.
stateKeys.packPatch: Fields that replace the named pack fields for this scenario.

scenarios.name: Chat home
scenarios.group: Two modes, one set of parts

content.blurb: Chat mode is the default face. Home is a composer with what needs you as cards above it and recent conversations below.

expect: The main area shows a composer with Needs you cards above it and a Recent conversations list below it.
The Needs you heading shows the same number as the My work count on the rail.
The rail shows the tenant mark as Home, the mode switch, My work, Conversations, and Browse in that order, with the avatar last.
No pack destination appears on the rail in Chat mode.

scenarios.name: A conversation with the Assistant
scenarios.group: Two modes, one set of parts

content.blurb: A conversation with the Assistant is a stream whose answer carries a live list bound to a query, not a pasted snapshot. The change it suggests is a proposal with before and after values.

expect: The stream header shows context chips for the current place and a record, each with a remove button, plus an Add chip.
The answer contains a list labeled Live with an Open in tab control.
The proposal shows Before and After values for each affected record, and nothing changes until someone who can approve it does.
Messages from the Assistant carry an agent label in text.
The composer says that / runs an action from the action catalog.

scenarios.name: A team conversation
scenarios.group: Two modes, one set of parts

content.blurb: People and agents share one kind of conversation. The Assistant joins by @mention, and status changes on records show in the stream as events.

expect: Messages from people, a system event for a record status change, and an Assistant reply appear in one stream in time order.
A record mentioned in the conversation is offered with an Add to context control and is not added to the context chips on its own.
The conversation sidebar groups rows under Pinned, Recent, and a user section, with All, People, Agents, and Places filters.
The open conversation row is marked as the current page.

scenarios.name: A record in Chat mode
scenarios.group: Two modes, one set of parts

content.blurb: Every record is a stream. In Chat mode its conversation face fills the main area and Details opens as a panel tab.

expect: The main area shows the record's events and messages, with a composer addressed to everyone on the record.
The side panel holds one Details tab for the same record.
The Details button in the stream header focuses the existing Details tab instead of opening a second one.
The breadcrumb names the destination and the record id.

scenarios.name: Workspace mode
scenarios.group: Two modes, one set of parts

content.blurb: Workspace mode shows the same parts with the structured face first, with destinations on the rail, the list in the main area, and the record in a panel tab. Switching mode keeps your tabs.

expect: The rail lists My work, the pack destinations, a separator, the secondary destinations, and Conversations, in that order.
The main area shows the destination list under a context bar, and the record shows in a Details panel tab.
Switching to Chat mode and back keeps the same open tabs in the same order.
The mode switch is announced in a polite live region and focus stays on the mode button.
Activating a rail destination emits one activation request with its id, and the shell does no routing of its own.

scenarios.name: Browse
scenarios.group: Two modes, one set of parts

content.blurb: In Chat mode every list is one click away in Browse. Each list opens as a page, or as a panel tab from a conversation.

expect: Browse shows one card for each pack destination, primary and secondary.
Each card shows how many records the destination holds and its first two views.
The Browse rail item is marked as the current page.

scenarios.name: Workspace home
scenarios.group: Two modes, one set of parts

content.blurb: Workspace mode keeps the dashboard home, with conversations one click away.

expect: Home shows the pack figures as cards and a Needs you list whose length matches the My work count.
A Conversations card lists recent conversations as links.
The page title greets the user by first name.

scenarios.name: Rail labels

content.blurb: With rail labels on, the rail widens from 56 to 80 pixels and the avatar shows your first name.

expect: The rail is 80 pixels wide and every rail item shows its short label under the icon.
The avatar button shows the user's first name, and its accessible name includes the tenant.
Turning labels off returns the rail to 56 pixels with icons only and the same accessible names.

scenarios.name: First run

content.blurb: Before any work exists, no counts appear anywhere and Home says what it is for.

expect: No count appears on the rail or on Home.
Home welcomes the user to the tenant by first name and says nothing needs them yet.
Starter chips name the tenant and the first destination.

scenarios.name: Phone drawer

content.blurb: On a phone there is no rail, and the drawer carries the same items with the needs-you count as a number. Each device class remembers its own mode.

expect: No rail renders at 390 pixels, and a menu button opens the drawer.
The drawer lists Home, My work, Conversations, and Browse, with the My work count shown as a number.
The menu button's accessible name includes the needs-you count.
Choosing a mode on a phone leaves the mode remembered for laptop width unchanged.

scenarios.name: Tabs of many kinds

content.blurb: The side panel is a tab host where a tab is a kind plus a target, so two records can stay open side by side. Pinned tabs shrink to icons, the rest shrink and then scroll, and the chevron searches every open tab.

expect: The tab strip is a tablist, and the pinned Assistant tab shows as an icon while keeping its name for assistive technology.
Details tabs for two different records are open at once, and opening Details for a record that already has one focuses that tab.
The preview tab is set in italics and its title and subline also say preview in text.
The chevron control's name gives the number of open tabs, and it lists every open tab.
Opening or closing a tab is announced in a polite live region without moving focus.

scenarios.name: Preview tab follows the list

content.blurb: Clicking a row, or pressing J or K while the list has focus, moves the preview tab, shown in italics, to that record. Keep open, Pin, or an edit makes the tab stay.

expect: Selecting another row retargets the preview tab instead of opening a new tab.
J and K move the selection only while the list has focus.
Keep open turns the preview tab into a kept tab and drops its italics and its preview text.
The row shown in the panel carries aria-current.

scenarios.name: New tab

content.blurb: New tab offers the kinds that apply here, suggestions from the selection, and tabs you closed.

expect: Tools lists only the kinds the pack allows for this record kind, plus Page and Assistant.
Suggested offers a Timeline for the selected record and a conversation about it.
Recents lists the closed Log tab, and choosing it reopens that tab.
No inapplicable kind appears, disabled or otherwise.

scenarios.name: A tab that doesn't apply

content.blurb: The preview Files tab followed the selection to a record kind with no files. It stays and says why instead of vanishing.

expect: The Files tab stays in the strip, and its body says this record kind does not have files.
The message names the selected record and offers Show Details instead.
The tab leaves the strip only when the user closes it.

scenarios.name: Log

content.blurb: Log lists a record's events and messages in order, filtered by People, System, or Agents. Agent actions name who proposed and who approved.

expect: Log shows All, People, System, and Agents filters, with All pressed.
Choosing Agents leaves only the Assistant's entry, which says it proposed a change that the current user approved.
Agent and system entries carry a text label, not only a color.

scenarios.name: Timeline

content.blurb: Timeline is a time axis that shows spans, overlaps, and planned work. The order of events lives in Log.

expect: Timeline shows month labels and one bar per span, with planned work marked planned in text.
A Today marker sits on the axis.
The timeline has a text alternative that describes its spans.

scenarios.name: A page

content.blurb: Pages are lasting documents in a tree. A change the Assistant suggests shows inline to accept or reject, with attribution.

expect: The page tree lists the pack pages with the open page marked.
The suggested change shows the removed and the inserted text, labeled as AI, with Accept and Reject controls.
The page names who wrote it, including the Assistant.

scenarios.name: Results ready

content.blurb: A job you started finished while Open results when ready was on and the panel was visible, so its output tab opened. The output stays a draft until you save it to a record or a page.

expect: An Output tab opens after the Details tab and becomes the active tab.
The output is labeled as a draft not saved anywhere yet, with Save to the record, Save as page, and Discard.
Focus stays where it was when the tab opens, and the opening is announced politely.
With Open results when ready off, the finished job adds a My work item and a badge instead of opening a tab.

scenarios.name: Two tab groups

content.blurb: When there is room, a tab can move into a second group. Nothing forces Details and the Assistant side by side.

expect: Two panel groups render at 1920 pixels, and the second holds the Assistant tab.
Each group has its own tablist and its own active tab.
The second group offers Merge this group back.
Search tabs lists the tabs of both groups and marks those in group 2.

scenarios.name: Floating when space is short

content.blurb: At 1024 pixels a docked panel would leave the list about 348 pixels, so the panel floats. It docks only when the main area keeps 560 pixels.

expect: The panel floats over a scrim instead of docking beside the list.
The list keeps its full width behind the panel.
Clicking the scrim or pressing Esc closes the panel and returns focus to the control that opened it.
The same state at 1440 pixels docks the panel.

scenarios.name: Tabs on a phone

content.blurb: On a phone the panel is a bottom sheet, and its tabs show as a grid.

expect: The panel renders as a bottom sheet.
A button that names the tab count opens a grid with one card per open tab and a New tab card.
Choosing a card makes that tab active.

scenarios.name: Search open

content.blurb: One box finds and asks. Enter opens the highlighted row, Ctrl Enter asks, and Tab only moves between controls.

expect: Search opens as a modal dialog with focus in the input.
With an empty query it shows Recent items, a New action for each pack kind, and an Ask the Assistant row.
Enter acts on the highlighted row, and Ctrl Enter always asks the Assistant.
Tab moves focus between controls and never changes the highlighted row.
Esc closes the dialog and returns focus to the Ask box.

scenarios.name: Results by kind

content.blurb: While you type, results group by kind, and Ask the Assistant is the last row.

expect: Results group under one heading per record kind, with an All filter and one filter per kind.
Ask the Assistant is the last row and quotes the query.
The scope chip names the current place, and the footer says in: limits results to a place.

scenarios.name: A question

content.blurb: When what you typed reads as a question, asking comes first.

expect: Ask the Assistant is the first row and is highlighted.
Record results follow under a Records heading.
Enter asks, because the highlighted row is the ask row.

scenarios.name: Shortcuts

content.blurb: Shortcuts are data, so the shortcut sheet and the remap setting read the same table. The shell binds no single letters, and the tab keys avoid the ones browsers reserve.

expect: The sheet is a modal dialog that lists each shortcut and what it does.
No shell shortcut is a single letter, and J and K are listed as working only while a list has focus.
Panel tab shortcuts are Ctrl Alt T and Ctrl Alt W, not Ctrl T or Ctrl W.
The sheet says any shortcut can be remapped or turned off in Settings.

scenarios.name: Context bar

content.blurb: Status tabs sit on the left, with Filter, Sort, the view switch, and New on the right. Filter covers text contains, so there is no second search box.

expect: The context bar shows the destination status tabs, then Filter, Sort, the view switch when there is more than one view, and New.
The Filter control's accessible name says it includes text contains, and no second search box appears.
New names the destination record kind and is the only primary button in the bar.
The sidebar scope chip names the current place with a Last used tag.

scenarios.name: Selection bar

content.blurb: While rows are selected, the selection bar replaces the context bar. Its actions come from the same catalog as every other action surface.

expect: The bar reads 2 selected and offers the catalog actions for the selection.
The context bar is not shown while rows are selected.
Esc clears the selection before it closes anything beneath it.

scenarios.name: My work

content.blurb: The count is only what needs you. Mentions, finished work, and notices sit below as Updates and never add to it.

expect: The Needs you heading shows the same number as the rail count.
Updates lists mentions, status changes, and notices without a count.
Each needs-you row carries a Needs you tag in text, and counts use the attention color, never the danger color.
The rail count is part of the My work item's accessible name.

scenarios.name: Working in the background

content.blurb: A job runs while the panel is closed. Progress shows in the Ask box, and a badge sits on the panel toggle.

expect: The Ask box shows the job verb and its progress as done of total.
The panel toggle shows a numeric badge.
The panel does not open and focus does not move while the job runs.
When the job finishes, it is announced politely and becomes a My work item.

scenarios.name: Offline

content.blurb: Work goes on offline, and the strip says what is still only on this device.

expect: A status strip says Offline and how many changes are still on this device.
Items not sent yet are marked with the words not sent yet, not only an icon or a color.
The list status bar says Offline and how many changes are not sent.
The list and its actions stay usable.

scenarios.name: A conflict

content.blurb: Nothing is overwritten. A conflict shows in the strip and becomes a My work item.

expect: The strip says 1 change needs a decision, names the record, and says nothing was overwritten.
The strip offers a Review button.
My work gains a Sync conflict item, and the count rises by one.

scenarios.name: Out of date

content.blurb: The app never says Synced. When the last confirmation is old, the strip says how old.

expect: The strip reads Last confirmed 3 hours ago and offers Try now.
The words Synced and Up to date never appear.
The relative age and the clock time are formatted for the active locale from the recency the API returns.

scenarios.name: Avatar menu

content.blurb: The avatar menu shows who you are, the tenants you belong to with what needs you in each, Settings, sync, help, and Sign out last. Picking a tenant switches everything to that tenant.

expect: The avatar button opens a menu, and its accessible name includes the user, the tenant, and account menu.
The menu header names the user, role, and tenant, and tenants are menu item radios with the current one checked.
Other tenants show their needs-you counts as numbers inside the menu only.
Sign out is the last item.
Choosing another tenant replaces the open tabs, mode, and place with that tenant's own, and nothing carries across.

scenarios.name: One tenant

content.blurb: With one tenant the switcher section disappears, and the header still names the tenant.

expect: The menu shows no tenant list.
The menu header still names the role and the tenant.
Settings, Sync, Help and shortcuts, and Sign out keep their order.

scenarios.name: An account action

content.blurb: The avatar badge counts account actions only, such as signing in again before an offline lease ends.

expect: The avatar shows a badge of 1, and its accessible name includes 1 account action.
The first item after the menu header is Sign in again before Friday.
Needs-you counts from other tenants do not add to the avatar badge.

scenarios.name: Settings

content.blurb: One Settings surface is sectioned by scope. Every value says where it comes from, and a lock means the organization set it.

expect: Settings shows You, This device, and Workspace, and Organization appears only for people who can change it.
Every value shows its source in text, and a locked value also shows a lock.
Mode shows the role default and says the user can change it.
Back returns to the tenant.

scenarios.name: This device

content.blurb: Because the app is offline first, what happens to this device's data is set here, not decided at sign-out.

expect: This device lists Shared device, When I sign out, Offline storage, Last confirmed, and Remove this device's data.
Shared device is locked and says the tenant set it.
Remove this device's data is a button that asks before it acts.

scenarios.name: Focus mode

content.blurb: In Focus mode the rail, sidebar, and panel leave. A slim bar offers the panels back and exits with Esc.

expect: No rail, sidebar, or panel renders.
The header shows a Focus tag, a Panels button, and Exit focus with Esc.
Esc exits focus mode only when no higher layer is open.

scenarios.name: Tablet

content.blurb: At tablet width the header stays the same but tighter. Share loses its label, the sidebar goes, and the rail stays.

expect: The rail renders and the destination sidebar does not.
Share shows only its icon and keeps the accessible name Share.
Tab order follows the visual order of rail, header, context bar, and list.

scenarios.name: Shell structure

content.blurb: Sets up the neutral pack in Workspace mode with a shell id and one host attribute, to check landmarks and what the shell leaves to its host.

expect: The shell root carries data-shell-id set to example-shell and the host data-case attribute.
One rail navigation landmark, one header, and one main region render.
Every label, count, and row comes from the pack, and the shell adds only chrome labels from its catalog.
In forced colors every control boundary and the current item stay visible.

scenarios.name: Missing shell id

content.blurb: Sets up the neutral pack with no shell id.

expect: Rendering raises app-shell-id-required.
No partial shell renders.

scenarios.name: Duplicate destination id

content.blurb: Sets up the neutral pack with two destinations that share the id records.

expect: Rendering raises duplicate-nav-identity.
The error names the repeated id records.

scenarios.name: Nested destination

content.blurb: Sets up the neutral pack with a destination that nests another destination inside it.

expect: Rendering raises unsupported-nav-shape.
Nothing nested renders as a rail item.

scenarios.name: Denied actions

content.blurb: Sets up a selection where the API returns one action available, one disabled with a reason, and one hidden, and hides the Admin destination.

actions.reason: Only the owner can change status.

expect: Assign is enabled, Change status is disabled and shows the server reason in text, and Export is absent.
Admin does not appear on the rail, in Browse, or in search.
The shell derives no availability from the user role.

scenarios.name: Contribution validation

content.blurb: Sets up three pack contributions, one valid, one for an unknown contribution point, and one with an unsupported schema version.

expect: The record tab list contribution applies, so records offer only Details and Log.
The unknown point and the unsupported schema version are skipped.
Each skipped contribution produces one diagnostic that names its id and the reason.
The rest of the pack renders as if the skipped contributions were absent.

scenarios.name: Admin arrangement

content.blurb: Sets up an organization arrangement that hides the Timeline tab and a user arrangement that hides Files, then opens New tab.

expect: New tab offers neither Timeline nor Files.
An arrangement can hide or reorder pack contributions but never adds one the pack did not declare.
Settings shows each arrangement value with its source.

scenarios.name: Behavior flag off

content.blurb: Sets up a wide window with the tenant flag for panel tab groups turned off.

expect: At 1920 pixels there is room for two groups, yet no Move this tab to a second group control renders.
With the flag on, the same state shows the control.
The flag value comes from the tenant, not from the user or the pack.

scenarios.name: Minimum harness revision

content.blurb: Sets up the neutral pack declaring that it needs harness revision 7.

expect: The shell does not load the pack and reports a diagnostic that names revision 7 and the running revision 6.
No partial pack content renders.

scenarios.name: Restore saved tabs

content.blurb: Sets up injectable storage holding a saved record for this user and workspace with a pinned tab, a kept tab, and a preview tab.

expect: Defaults paint first, then the saved mode and tabs apply in one update.
The pinned and kept tabs come back, and the preview tab resets when the destination changes.
Each restored tab reloads through the permission check before it shows content.
A mode controlled by the host wins over the restored mode.

scenarios.name: Unreadable saved state

content.blurb: Sets up injectable storage whose saved record cannot be parsed.

expect: The shell renders its declared defaults.
No error is shown to the user.
An old record version or a failing read behaves the same way.

scenarios.name: Workspace switcher

content.blurb: Sets up nine workspaces in the rail switcher with the third active, two pinned, a long active name, and a directory entry, then opens the switcher.

workspaces.label: Workspace 3 with a long name that cannot fit the trigger

expect: The trigger shows the active workspace name on one line, truncated, with the full name still available.
The menu lists the active workspace first, then the pinned workspaces in pin order, then the rest.
A filter input appears because there are more than seven workspaces.
All workspaces is the menu footer.
Choosing a workspace emits one change request, closes the menu, and returns focus to the trigger.

scenarios.name: One workspace

content.blurb: Sets up a single workspace.

expect: No workspace switcher renders on the rail.
The remaining rail zones keep their order.

scenarios.name: Pinned views

content.blurb: Sets up the Mine view of Records as the only pin.

expect: Mine renders once under Pinned, and the Views list omits it.
Each pin toggle sits beside its item, is at least 44 pixels, and is reachable by keyboard.
Activating a pin toggle neither navigates nor moves focus off the toggle.
Unpinning returns the view to its place in the Views list.

scenarios.name: Pin cap and orphaned pin

content.blurb: Sets up eight stored pins, the cap, where records/archived-2024 names a view the pack no longer has.

expect: Seven pins render, and the orphaned pin does not.
The orphaned pin stays in storage so it returns if the view comes back.
With eight pins stored, a pin toggle on an unpinned view emits no request.

scenarios.name: Rename a conversation

content.blurb: Sets up a direct conversation in Chat mode with its sidebar row in inline rename.

expect: The row shows a text field holding the current title, with focus in it.
Enter emits a rename request with the new title, and the shell does not commit the value itself.
Escape emits a cancel request and returns focus to the row.
While the field has focus, J and K type text, and Enter and Escape go to the field rather than the shell.

scenarios.name: Conversation actions menu

content.blurb: Sets up the actions menu of a team conversation row, opened from its More button.

expect: The row More button opens a menu of conversation actions.
Destructive actions sit after a divider at the end of the menu.
Esc or a click outside closes the menu and returns focus to the More button.

scenarios.name: Shortcut guards

content.blurb: Sets up focus in the conversation composer, with Ctrl Alt W turned off in the user's shortcut settings.

expect: With focus in the composer, typing J or K enters text and moves no selection.
With focus in the composer, Ctrl K still opens search and Ctrl Shift I still hides the panel.
Ctrl Alt W closes no tab and shows as off on the shortcut sheet.
An event the focused control already handled triggers no shell shortcut.

scenarios.name: English locale

content.blurb: English chrome frames the neutral pack in Workspace mode with a record open in the panel.

expect: Every chrome label comes from the en-US catalog.
React and Blazor produce the same landmarks, accessible names, and order.

scenarios.name: Pseudo locale

content.blurb: Expanded pseudo-localized chrome labels check truncation without clipping the shell.

expect: Expanded labels truncate inside tabs, rail labels, and switcher triggers without clipping any control.
No chrome string is left unlocalized.

scenarios.name: Arabic locale

content.blurb: Arabic direction places the rail, sidebar, and panel on logical edges, with the sync strip showing an old confirmation.

expect: The rail sits on the inline-start edge and the panel on the inline-end edge.
Safe-area insets apply to the logical edges.
The sync strip formats its relative age and clock time in Arabic.

scenarios.name: Light theme

content.blurb: Light public tokens render the shell with a record in the panel and a sync conflict in the strip.

expect: Text, icons, and control boundaries meet contrast against the theme tokens.
Shell scroll regions use themed scrollbars whose thumb meets 3:1 against its surface.
Needs-you counts use the attention color, and only the conflict uses a danger state.
With reduced motion, the panel and menus appear without sliding.

scenarios.name: Dark theme

content.blurb: Dark public tokens keep the same hierarchy and affordances as the light theme.

expect: Text, icons, and control boundaries meet contrast against the theme tokens.
Shell scroll regions use themed scrollbars whose thumb meets 3:1 against its surface.
Needs-you counts use the attention color, and only the conflict uses a danger state.
With reduced motion, the panel and menus appear without sliding.

scenarios.name: Long content

content.blurb: Sets up every pack label lengthened to 120 characters and 24 open tabs.

expect: Long titles truncate or wrap with the full text still available, and no control overlaps another.
Tabs shrink to their minimum width and the strip then scrolls, keeping the active tab in view.
Conversation rows keep the title to one line and keep the unread count visible.

scenarios.name: Shell under load

content.blurb: Sets up 256 navigation items and 96 sequential state updates.

expect: React and Blazor resolve the 256 items into the same rail, sidebar, and search observations.
After 96 updates there is still one landmark set and no repeated live announcement.

scenarios.name: Two hundred open tabs

content.blurb: Sets up 200 open panel tabs.

expect: The strip scrolls and Search tabs lists all 200 tabs.
Opening a kind and target that is already open still focuses the existing tab.
